_comment: Export admissions for packages/principles-core. Schema and rules: scripts/check-core-export-surface.mjs. Every record needs expiresAt; consumers are parsed and must import AND use the symbol.

admissions.whyNotInternal: Console and CLI packages must resolve the two workspace database paths; without a public subpath every consumer keeps its own '.pd' / '.state' path.join literal, which is exactly the drift this batch removes.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Re-exporting the resolvers from the wide ./runtime barrel, rejected because that entry already carries 2,032 symbols and this batch must not widen it.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The console runs in a separate package that cannot import core-internal relative modules; it needs the single workspace-state path authority at runtime.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Copying the '.pd/state.db' literal in each console model, rejected because that keeps 20+ independent path authorities.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The console opens trajectory.db directly for read-only counts and pain lookups; it cannot reach the core-internal storage-paths module by relative import.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Importing it from ./trajectory-store, rejected because that entry is the trajectory API surface, not the workspace path contract.

admissions.whyNotInternal: pd-cli workspace discovery and the OpenClaw plugin's compatibility path layer need the canonical workspace-relative directory names in a separate package; without them each consumer re-derives '.pd'/'.state'/'memory' literals, which is the drift this convergence removes (PRI-1270).
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Keeping only the two db-path resolvers public was rejected: pd-config-loader builds the config path from PD_DIRS/PD_FILES and would have to hardcode the '.pd' directory literal again.

admissions.whyNotInternal: pd-cli config discovery and the OpenClaw plugin compatibility layer need the canonical workspace file map (config.yaml/state.db/trajectory.db) in a separate package; duplicating the map is exactly the second-path-authority this batch eliminates.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Exposing only resolvePdPath without the map was rejected: the plugin compatibility layer re-exports the map for its own modules and the CLI needs the raw names for legacy-file detection.

admissions.whyNotInternal: pd-cli resolves the workspace config path through the same Windows/POSIX join rules as the hosts; resolving it per-consumer with local path.join re-created platform-divergent path authorities.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Using resolveStateDbPath for config.yaml too was rejected: it hardcodes the state.db filename and cannot express the workspace-relative file map.

admissions.whyNotInternal: host-runtime owns the live decision gate in a separate package and cannot use a core-internal relative import; this subpath is the single input-assembly contract shared with Golden Trace replay, so the two paths cannot derive workspace.isRiskPath differently.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Re-exporting through the wide ./runtime barrel was rejected: it widens an already large public surface and hides which contract the host actually needs.

admissions.whyNotInternal: Provider keys are resolved in five separate processes (console, host-runtime classifier/selection, pd-cli probe and rule-host). They live in different packages and cannot import a core-internal module; without one shared resolver each process keeps its own env lookup and the local credentials file silently stops working for the agents the Owner configured.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Adding apiKey values to .pd/config.yaml was rejected: ADR-0016 still forbids secret fields in config.yaml, and the validator keeps rejecting them. Duplicating the file reader per process was rejected because it recreates the precedence rule (env first) and the YAML schema in every consumer.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The console runs in a separate package and cannot import the core-internal pi-ai catalog bridge. It needs the same read-only projection the runtime already trusts, otherwise the picker would ship a second, hand-maintained provider/model list.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Importing @earendil-works/pi-ai directly in pd-console was rejected: the catalog entry shapes would then be interpreted twice (adapter and console), and the console would drift from the runtime's provider validation.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The console route must run the exact same provider/model resolution and transport classification the runtime uses; a console-local HTTP probe would validate a different code path than the one that actually runs agents.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Calling `pd runtime probe` as a subprocess was rejected: it adds a process boundary, a second error serialization format, and cannot classify model-list vs chat stages without parsing CLI text.

admissions.whyNotInternal: Stage-2 classification runs in two other packages (the shared host-runtime classifier factory and the OpenClaw plugin host that owns the trajectory). Both must construct and pass the same fact shape into the core-owned prompt builder; a relative core-internal import is not possible across packages, and duplicating the shape would create a second contract for the same evidence.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Inlining a structural type in each consumer was rejected: the prompt builder and the gate would then accept shapes no shared type constrains, which is exactly how the R3 'no behavioral fact' misclassification reached admission.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The console renders the approval card in a separate package and must read the SAME server verdict the approval write path enforces; re-deriving the gate in the console would create a second authority that can promise an approval the server refuses.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Re-deriving the conflict verdict in the console model from the artifact JSON was rejected: it duplicates the resolution-binding rules and would drift from the write path that actually blocks the approval.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The value above crosses the package boundary, so its shape must too; a console-local structural copy would silently accept fields the producer removed.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Duplicating the interface in pd-console was rejected: the console would keep compiling after the gate projection changes, hiding a real contract break.

admissions.whyNotInternal: Both Dreamer seeding entry points live in pd-cli (the diagnose seed loop and the review-create/backfill seed paths) while the bridge seeds from core; a resolved-to-existing or reuse-parked candidate must get the SAME suppression verdict in every entry point, and that verdict must derive from persistent ledger identity + admission processing, not a transient intake result — so the guard has to be one shared function crossing the package boundary.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Re-implementing the two-fact check inline in each pd-cli entry point was rejected: four copies (diagnose, review-create, backfill, bridge) would drift, and the 19aa989d production anomaly (consumed AND parked AND seeded) came exactly from seeding decisions that did not consult persistent identity.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The suppression verdict crosses the package boundary with the function, so its result shape must too; a pd-cli-local structural copy would keep compiling after the guard adds a suppression reason.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Returning a bare boolean was rejected: the CLI must report WHICH durable fact suppressed the seed (resolved onto principle X vs park pending), and a boolean erases that observability.

admissions.whyNotInternal: Phase A intent construction lives in the pd-cli review service (the only caller that owns the verified Owner identity context), while the decisionId formula and policy stamp are the admission document's own contract in core — exporting the builder keeps one implementation instead of duplicating the hash formula in pd-cli.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Rejected: exporting only the decisionId hash formula (or duplicating it in pd-cli) — two implementations of the identity contract could drift; the builder keeps one.

admissions.whyNotInternal: Every Dreamer seeding entry point and the review service must read the SAME pending-decision verdict from the admission document as the intake service does in core; a core-internal-only helper would force each caller to re-implement the scan.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Rejected: exposing the raw ownerDecisions array type alone and letting each caller scan it — four callers would re-implement the same newest-pending scan.

admissions.whyNotInternal: Phase A resume/already-applied detection in the pd-cli review service reads the applied record to report a completed decision without re-executing it (crash-recovery contract).
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Rejected: reading the raw document in pd-cli and filtering executionStatus by hand — the newest-applied selection rule would live in two packages.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The typed decision record crosses the package boundary as the store method parameter/return; pd-cli cannot reference it without the export.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Rejected: pd-cli-local mirror of the record shape — a second truth for the lifecycle fields the core store validates.

admissions.whyNotInternal: Host-runtime (and through it pd-cli, codex-adapter, workbuddy-adapter) must evaluate the single intent_engineering predicate against the ENTRY-provided effectiveConfig; core owns the predicate so no entry re-implements the flag decision (SPEC-PD-INTENT-UNIFICATION-001 §9.3 rule 5).
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Re-exporting computeFeatureFlagsFromConfig and re-deriving the flag per consumer, rejected because SPEC §7.2/P2-2 requires ONE predicate for the whole anchoring chain; a second derivation is exactly the drift the unification removed.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The console summary/save responses must project per-section authored/placeholder/missing states from the SAME deterministic classifier Stage A and the prompt hook use; a console-local copy would create a second template-matching truth (SPEC §7.1 shared pure function).
admissions.alternativeConsidered: A console-local regex classifier, rejected: SPEC §7.1/§12.2 explicitly forbid re-implementing classification in the UI layer.

admissions.whyNotInternal: Document-level readiness (template_only/incomplete/configured) must be derived by the one shared function so the API counts cannot disagree with Stage A snapshot gating.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Counting authored sections inline in the model, rejected: the not_configured/partially/configured thresholds are contract, not display logic.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The sectionStates DTO type is the return element type of analyzeIntentDocSections; the console model types its projection with it so an upstream enum change is a compile error, not a silent shape drift.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Re-declaring the union locally, rejected: a second union drifts from the classifier contract silently.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The Intent wizard runs in the browser bundle and imports from the browser-safe subpath; it must classify user input with the SAME deterministic function the server uses post-save, or the wizard finish summary can label template text as 已填写 while the saved state says placeholder (PR #2684 review).
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Duplicating the classifier in the console, rejected: SPEC §7.1 requires exactly one shared classification; a second copy is the drift this PR removes.

admissions.alternativeConsidered: Duplicating the classifier in the console, rejected: SPEC §7.1 requires exactly one shared classification; a second copy is the drift this PR removes.
